mission.title: Incommunicado
mission.description: Find out what the Exiles know about the commandos.

npc.say: Didn't you hear me, wuss? I said, get out of here! You can't make me talk!
You'd better leave. You don't want to see my husband when he's really mad.

phase.briefing:
Warrior, as you know, Commander Lock has given orders that we are to avoid initiating hostilities against the commandos. Fortunately, no such restriction applies to our interactions with the Merovingian's Exiles. We know that meetings have taken place between the two parties, so it seems likely that the Exiles know things about the commandos that we do not.
We would like to know what the Exiles know about the commandos. I'm sending you to rendezvous with one of our neighborhood intelligence officers, Bulgakov. He'll direct you to an Exile group that has met with the commandos recently.

enter.say: That's the building where you're meeting Bulgakov.

talk.say: {player}? Right, right. Okay, there's an Exile gang around here that we spotted meeting with a commando squad. The Exile leader's name is Agassiz. I'll have my boys beam their coordinates up to your operator. Good luck, soldier!

phase.briefing: I'm glad to hear that you're making progress, {player}. You'll probably have to get the information out of the Exile leader, Agassiz. Use whatever means seem necessary--this information is of vital importance to Zion!

enter.say: I'm reading multiple Exile signals in there. No security system, as far as I can see.

talk.say: Well, well, look what the code dragged in. If you're looking for Agassiz, I'm afraid he isn't here right now; but if you're looking for a painful exit from this simulation, I think I can oblige you.
I was afraid of that. Maybe someone there has a clue to Agassiz's current whereabouts.

done.say: Check Buffer's body, bwana. The code stream is showing that he's got a document of some sort.
Aha, it seems that they have a secondary base. Maybe we'll find Agassiz there. Head out and I'll update your waypoint.

phase.briefing: Stay on his trail, Warrior. We need Agassiz's information!

enter.say: I'm picking up lots of Exiles in there. Hopefully one of them is Agassiz. They've got a security system, too.

I've finished scanning that entire area, and there's no program in there that matches Agassiz's profile. So this is a dead end, unless you can find a clue to his present location.
The computer in that room is password-protected; if you need an access code, check around for their security mainframe.

done.say: Good; now, search that computer. Maybe it holds a clue to Agassiz's location.
Looks like they had a phone number for him stored away on there. Get that disk and upload it to me; I'll see if I can track the number to a new address.

objective.text: Upload the Disk at a hardline

done.say: Cool. Tracing it now. I should have a new waypoint for you shortly.

phase.briefing: You're close to finding Agassiz, {player}; I can feel it. Do whatever you have to do to get him to reveal what he's learned about the commandos.

enter.say: That's where the number led...but do Exiles really live in apartments, like everyday bluepills? Somehow I never thought about it before. If Agassiz is at home, he might be less than pleased to have you knocking down his front door.

talk.say: Hah! You want information? Well, what are you gonna do about it, you Zion puppy? Slaughter me in my own home? Even if you could, that wouldn't get you the information you want, would it? Piss off.
What a pompous ass! He might be right, though. If only there were some way to make him talk--something he values that you could use as leverage...

Hey-- Ow! You big jerk! First you come busting in here without an invitation, then you try slapping me around in my own home? Fine, I'll follow you, but my husband, Agassiz, will give you hell for it if he catches you!

Careful, {player}. Mrs. Branson is a bluepill. It's unusual for a bluepill to have married an Exile gang leader, but nevertheless, Zion is pledged to protect bluepills to the best of our ability. Do not allow Mrs. Branson to come to harm.
You don't know who you're messing with, creep!

done.say:
So! Threatening my wife in my own home, are you? I didn't think you Zion pus-bags had the stones to pull something this devious! Hmm... Fine.
All I can tell you is what the commandos told me: they're obsolete military programs who came into the Matrix to avoid deletion by the Machines. They offered us an alliance, or at least a mutual non-interference agreement.
That's it. Now get this: if I ever see you again, you'll find out how a jacked-in redpill can die by an overload of simulated pain. Get out of my home!

objective.text: Do not let Tandra Branson die

mission.finish:
That was a dangerous game, {player}; I'm just glad that nobody was hurt. Then again, Mrs. Branson has apparently succeeded in domesticating an Exile leader, so perhaps she knows what she's doing.
I think we can trust the information that Agassiz gave you, since part of it corresponded with intelligence you uncovered in a previous mission. If the commandos really are old military programs from the Machine world, as it seems they claim, they could be very valuable allies--or very dangerous enemies.
I will report this information to Commander Lock immediately. Zion thanks you for your efforts today, Warrior.
